newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to permit bond stripping from middle 1997.
newsitem.headline: Germany to permit bond stripping from middle 1997.

text.p: The German government on Friday unveiled a key change in the way its debt can be traded, bringing it into line with international standards and further improving Germany's status as a leading financial centre.

In a long awaited move, the Bundesbank said Germany would allow bond dealers to strip 10- and 30-year bonds from July 1997. This means the bond can be split into its principal and its coupon. The two are then sold separately with the principal a zero-coupon security.
The Bundesbank is the government's issuing agent.

"This step is absolutely necessary to help Germany reach an international standard and give German banks some experience in dealing with this business before Europe's currency union is slated to begin," said Armin Kayser, analyst at SBC Warburg in Frankfurt.

Bond stripping has not been permitted in Germany, and analysts say it has put the market at a disadvantage with the United States and some European nations where the practice has been used for some time.

Analysts said the government announced the measure one half-year before it becomes effective in order to give banks an opportunity to prepare for the step. But they said they had no idea why it had taken the government so long to finally agree to the measure.
"Of course we welcome the move, but it comes very late in the game," Kayser added.
In the first quarter 1997, the government plans to issue a total of up to 54 billion marks in new debt, the Bundesbank said.
At the same time the Bundesbank said Bonn would issue a strippable 30-year bond in the middle of the year which it plans to top up at a later date.

Both the government's already issued 6.25 percent bond maturing 2024 and the new year's bond of 1997 would also be strippable, the Bundesbank said. It has set January 4 and July 4 as dates when issues can be stripped.

The Bundesbank also said the government plans to issue one 10-year bond with a volume of up to 15 billion marks in the first ten days of January and top up the issue, with a volume of up to 10 billion marks in the third ten days of January.
